gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each 25,000 mAh bank's headline watts become in use: the INIU P63's "100 W" held for only 30-35 minutes in smartzone's test, falls to 65 W + 35 W with a second USB-C device, delivered 75.7-78.7 Wh of its stated 92.5 Wh, and ships with a 60 W cable; and the UGREEN 145W sold today (140 W / 65 W ports, PPS listed) is not the 100 W / 45 W unit the 2023 reviews tested.
standout_why: Compared against dupple.com (cited), powerbanks.fyi under-$100 (cited) and 25,000mAh pages, techwithall.com's Anker 25K review, and UGREEN's and INIU's store listings; techradar.com/au returned only navigation, so it was not compared. Dupple already gives per-port watts for the UGREEN 145W (140/65/22.5), a 5 V rated capacity for the Sharge and "63 to 70 Wh usable" for the Anker, but no split for the UGREEN 145W or INIU and no measured capacity. Powerbanks.fyi prints one "Output" number per bank that mixes combined (UGREEN 145, 200) with single-port (INIU 100) figures. Techwithall has the Anker splits and "110W across two ports" for the INIU, with no testing. None has the INIU's measured Wh, its 100 W duration, its 60 W cable, or the UGREEN version change.
decides: Confirms the UGREEN 145W 25K ($59.98) over the INIU P63 ($66.99) for anyone charging a laptop. UGREEN's spec gives 140 W from one port; the INIU gives 100 W that smartzone saw drop to 65 W after 30-35 minutes or as soon as a second device is plugged in, and it needs a 5 A cable bought separately. The INIU keeps the weight segment only. Among "165-200 W" names, the Anker 25K and AOHi Black Warrior give one laptop 100 W; only the UGREEN 145W, UGREEN 200W and Baseus FC41 25K give one device 140 W.

findings.label: Maker's per-port spec (current unit)
findings.value: 25,000 mAh / 3.6 V / 90 Wh (TYP); USB-C1 out 140 W max (28 V 5 A); USB-C2 out 65 W max (20 V 3.25 A); USB-A 22.5 W max; USB-C1 in 65 W max
findings.note: Spec table on UGREEN's bundle listing for the same bank, read with storecheck. The "145 W" in the name is the combined figure; one port alone gives 140 W. The cables in this bundle are 100 W, so they cannot carry 140 W.

findings.label: PD version and PPS as UGREEN lists them
findings.value: Tab heading "PD3.1 140w"; USB-C1/C2 output protocols line reads "PD3.0/PD2.0/QC3.0/QC2.0/FCP/AFC/APPLE 5V2.4A/BC1.2/5V Adaptive/PPS"; PD3.1 is named only in the USB-C1 input line
findings.note: UGREEN's own table is inconsistent: it lists a 28 V 5 A (140 W) output but omits PD3.1 from the output protocols. PPS is listed for both USB-C outputs; no PPS voltage range is given.

findings.label: 2023 unit, as tested by smartzone (Jonas Andre, 2023-07-18)
findings.value: USB-C1 100 W, USB-C2 45 W, USB-A 18 W; just under 60 Wh delivered at a constant 12 W from USB-A, 68% of the stated 88.2 Wh; no PPS; 2 h 15 min to 98% on a 65 W charger; 507 g
findings.source_title: Ugreen PB205 im Test – Powerbank mit 25.000 mAh und 145W Leistung
findings.note: This is the older 100 W + 45 W version, so its 60 Wh and no-PPS results should not be attached to the 140 W / 65 W unit sold today. This explains why reviews disagree on PD 3.1 and PPS.

findings.value: C1+C2 100 W + 45 W (145 W max); C1+USB-A 100 W + 18 W; C2+USB-A 15 W max; all three 100 W + 15 W (115 W max); USB PD 3.0; no Samsung PPS at 25 W or 45 W
findings.note: Older version again (C1 100 W). I could not read a split table for the current 140 W unit.

findings.note: Read with storecheck search on iniushop.com. INIU's listing claims a 3-year warranty and "Charge 3 Devices at Once".

findings.label: Delivered capacity, measured by smartzone (Jan, 2025-03-31)
findings.value: 75.67 Wh at 100 W, 77.63 Wh at 65 W, 78.73 Wh at 27 W; 82%, 84% and 85% of the maker's 92.5 Wh
findings.source_title: INIU P63-E1 im Test – kompakte Powerbank mit 100W und 25.000 mAh
findings.note: Loads were 20 V 5 A, 20 V 3.25 A and 9 V 3 A. Arithmetic: $66.99 / 77.63 Wh = $0.86 per delivered Wh at 65 W; $66.99 / 92.5 Wh = $0.72 per stated Wh (UGREEN: $59.98 / 90 Wh = $0.67 per stated Wh).

findings.label: What "100 W" becomes in use, per smartzone (Jan)
findings.value: 100 W held for only 30-35 minutes, then 65 W with about 30% left; C1+C2 = 65 W + 35 W; C1+USB-A = 65 W + 22.5 W; all three = 65 W + 7.5 W + 7.5 W; bundled cable rated 3 A / 60 W
findings.source_title: INIU P63-E1 im Test – kompakte Powerbank mit 100W und 25.000 mAh
findings.note: Single-port maxima in the review: C1 100 W, C2 45 W, USB-A 22.5 W, PD 3.0. Other figures: 65 W input, 1 h 45 min full recharge, 390 g. A 5 A cable is needed to get 100 W at all.
